title: United Air Lines 553
summary: A Boeing 737 approaching Chicago Midway was too high on descent at the outer marker beacon. The captain extended spoilers and steepened descent to 1,550 feet per minute, well above the normal 1,000 fpm. After leveling at minimum descent altitude with engines not advanced fully and spoilers still extended, the aircraft entered an aerodynamic stall. The stick shaker activated and continued sounding until impact into a residential neighborhood. The flight data recorder was inoperative due to maintenance failure.
probable_cause: The captain's failure to exercise positive flight management during the execution of a nonprecision approach, which culminated in a critical deterioration of airspeed into the stall regime where level flight could no longer be maintained (p. 32).

factors.evidence: The flight was slow in responding to ATC requests for speed reductions and to the descent clearance (p. 32). The aircraft crossed the outer marker about 700 feet above the published minimum crossing altitude (p. 32).
There was a breakdown in crew coordination during the most critical phase of the approach (p. 32). The first officer did not make the prescribed altitude callouts during the approach (p. 32).

The captain did not call for the final descent check until the aircraft had passed the outer marker; the distance from the outer marker to the runway was 3.3 nmi (p. 32). The flight spoilers were deployed to the flight detent position for the final descent from the Kedzie OM and remained in this position during the level-off at MDA (p. 32).
The sound of stickshaker activation could be heard on the CVR tape beginning at 14:27:03, about 22 seconds before impact (p. 6).

The aircraft descended below the overcast in a nose-high attitude with the sound of high engine power just before impact (p. 2). Several survivors reported the aircraft shuddered following a nose-up pitch change, with some estimating the nose rose at least 30 degrees (p. 7).
The aircraft crashed into residential area approximately 1.5 miles southeast of the approach end of Runway 31L at 14:27:25 CST, destroyed by impact and subsequent fire (p. 1).

events.text: Captain called for final descent check at 14:26:24, about 4 seconds after the Kedzie OM identifier ended (p. 6).

Chicago Approach Control cleared UA-553 to descend to 2,000 feet at 14:23:42, after issuing multiple speed reduction requests starting at 14:21:56 to reduce airspeed to 180 knots then to 160 knots (p. 5-6).
UA-553 reported passing the Kedzie Outer Marker inbound; tower controller advised they were number two on approach and would keep them advised (p. 6).
First officer called 'Ah, thousand feet'; less than 2 seconds later, stickshaker activation could be heard on CVR tape, indicating approach to stall (p. 6).
Tower controller issued missed approach clearance to UA-553: 'United five fifty-three execute a missed approach, make a left turn to a heading of one eight zero climb to two thousand' (p. 6).
Approach controller noticed radar target had drifted approximately 1/8 to 1/4 mile to the right of localizer centerline, disappearing from radarscope shortly thereafter (p. 6).
Aircraft crashed into residential area approximately 1.5 miles southeast of runway approach end, destroyed by impact and subsequent fire (p. 1-2).
CVR recording ended at 14:27:25; stickshaker sound had been audible for entire approximately 22-second period from initial stall warning (p. 6).

recommendations.text: Reassess and improve the methods used, both in flight manuals and in simulator or flight training, to familiarize flightcrews with the effects of spoilers on aircraft characteristics and stall warning devices.
Issue an advisory bulletin to alert pilots and operators to the hazards of the improper use of spoilers.

notes: Events extracted from approach controller radar observations and CVR transcript
